key_insight: The paper establishes CsPbCl3 as a temperature-calibration benchmark for in-situ high-temperature XRD, enabling more reliable phase-stability measurements in inorganic perovskite halides.
engineering_relevance: Accurate true-sample temperature tracking improves interpretation of thermal stability and decomposition in perovskite solar-cell materials, especially when comparing candidate absorber and double-perovskite compositions.
method: Used ligand-assisted re-precipitation to synthesize CsPbCl3 baseline powders.
Applied in-situ temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction to track phase transitions and decomposition.
Used a control substrate and refinement-based temperature conversion to estimate true sample temperature.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that in-situ temperature-dependent XRD successfully identified phase transitions and decomposition temperatures for CsPbCl3 and enabled follow-on thermal-kineitic testing of Cs2AgSbCl6.
watch_item: Thermal conclusions depend strongly on correct calibration of the true sample temperature, so substrate choice, heating geometry, and reproducibility must be tightly controlled.
paper_title: Thermal Corrections and Analysis on the Phase Stability of CsPbCl3 and Cs2AgSbCl6 during In-Situ Thermal Treatment
